messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: SLO burn-rate alert for service=redwood-runtime triggered. window=30m burn=220% -> paging triggered to #eng-oncall. Link: https://telemetry.redwood/runbooks/slo-burn

sam_sre: on-call here, ack'ing. I'll pull traces and check customer-impacting errors first.

maria: on it with you, sam. Looking at traces now — high rps to /v1/generate with lots of 503s from inference pool A.

aj: saw the CPU/GPU throttle spike earlier in the cluster — might be autoscaler thrash. throwing metrics at the dashboard: 
```
rate(fetch_errors[5m]) by (model)
redis_latency_p95{env="prod"}
```

ryan.k: customer support flagged ~12 customers affected in last 20m, tickets coming in. We should estimate blast radius and consider temporary fallback to smaller model pool.

sam_sre: initial impact: increased 5xxs on text-generation endpoints, error-rate on customer-facing routes ~0.9% over 20m (above 0.3% SLO). Paging criteria held up.

elena: can we confirm whether cached KV-eviction is the cause? I see increased KV cache misses coincident with the spike.

maria: copying logs:
```
2026-03-15T18:12:05Z runtime: kv_cache: miss key=conv-12345
2026-03-15T18:12:06Z runtime: inference: enqueue latency 120ms -> 3s
2026-03-15T18:12:07Z lb: upstream 503 from node i-02..
```

sam_sre: mitigation plan: 1) scale inference pool B by +4 nodes (manual) 2) enable fallback routing to model-lite variant for tier-1 customers 3) temporary relax aggressive batching to reduce enqueue latency. I'll run these now.

aj: +1 on scaling, but autoscaler needs tuning. I can apply a short-term tweak to the HPA window and CPU thresholds once we stabilize.

devops-bot: Scaling action started: added 4 nodes to pool-B. PR #34567 kicked off auto-provision.

sam_sre: routing fallback enabled for tier-1 customers. Confirming trace fan-out now.

maria: enqueue latency dropping to ~180ms after scale, 503s decreasing. customer-impacting error-rate now ~0.25% over last 10m. Looks like mitigation worked. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: UPDATE: SLO burn alert still firing on multi-window evaluation: 5m burn=400%, 30m burn=210%, 3h burn=95%. Paging still active due to 5m window.

sam_sre: we need to discuss alerting policy post-incident. This incident exposed noisy short-window pages where transient spikes caused full-team pages. Let's use this thread for live decisions + postmortem action items.

maria: Agreed. Proposal: change paging criteria to require either: (A) 5m burn > 500% AND customer-impacting error-rate > 1% OR (B) 30m burn > 200% (any customer-impacting errors). This would reduce paging for tiny blips while preserving responsiveness for sustained problems.

aj: I'm in favor, but we also need multi-window evaluation for burn. Right now our rule triggers on the shortest window only. Suggest multi-window gating: evaluate 2m, 30m, 3h windows and only page when short AND medium agree, or when medium alone exceeds threshold. Example logic: page if (burn_2m > 400% AND burn_30m > 150%) OR (burn_30m > 200%).

ryan.k: from customer ops POV, paging on micro-glitches made noise; we only want pages when customers are actually impacted. Add a customer-impact tag (tickets>0 OR errors_from_customers>threshold) to the rule.

elena: we should also add a debounce: require the 5m window to be sustained for at least 2 consecutive evaluations (evaluation interval=1m) before paging. That prevents single sample flukes.

sam_sre: good. Let's convert proposals into concrete alert rule diffs to review. I'll draft a change for the paging rule and a separate tweak for HPA/autoscaler windows.

maria: Draft rule (will put in PR):
```yaml
alert: SLOBurn_Paging_v2
expr: |
  let burn_2m = slo_burn_rate{window="2m"};
  let burn_30m = slo_burn_rate{window="30m"};
  let tickets = increase(customer_ticket_count[30m]);
  ( (burn_2m > 4.0 and burn_30m > 1.5 and tickets > 0) or (burn_30m > 2.0) )
for: 2m # require sustained
annotations:
  runbook: https://telemetry.redwood/runbooks/slo-burn
  page: true
```

aj: for autoscaler HPA short-term tweak I'll set stabilizationWindowSeconds=180 and increase targetCPU from 70->80 in the autoscale manifest. We'll open a separate ticket to audit scaling policies.

devops-bot: PR created: https://git.redwood/infra/alerts/pulls/128 (SLOBurn_Paging_v2). CI lint OK.

sam_sre: immediate action items from live coordination:
- Maria: own alert PR, follow-up review with ops (owner: maria, due: 2026-03-17)
- Aj: short-term HPA tweak and autoscaler stabilization change (owner: aj, due: 2026-03-16)
- Ryan: compile customer impact list and update severity in postmortem (owner: ryan.k, due: 2026-03-17)
- Sam: update runbook to include multi-window gating and debounce notes, and add dashboard panels for burn windows (owner: sam_sre, due: 2026-03-18)

maria: I'll also add a dashboard row with side-by-side panels: burn_2m, burn_30m, burn_3h + tickets count + KV cache-miss rate. That should make triage faster.

elena: Suggest adding a synthetic canary for the /v1/generate customer path to detect degraded tail-latency before SLO burn escalates.

sam_sre: good idea — file a ticket for canary (ops/monitoring backlog).

aj: one more: we should consider adding an override policy for Dedicated customers — for them we may want stricter paging criteria (page sooner). We'll document per-customer paging tiers in the runbook.

maria: PR merged to staging branch. Plan to roll to prod after post-incident review.

ryan.k: customer comms draft: "We've mitigated an incident causing increased 5xxs on generation. We're tuning alerts and autoscaling to avoid noisy pages and reduce future customer impact." I'll post the template to #customer-success.

sam_sre: wrapping up: incident declared mitigated — moving to retrospective. Final notes: keep short-window pages for severity>high only, use multi-window gating + debounce for page decision, and update dashboards/runbooks.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Status=mitigated. Duration=38m. Incident link: https://telemetry.redwood/incidents/INC-2026-0315-12

maria: filing postmortem ticket now and assigning owners. Thanks all on call. :clap: 

aj: thanks team. I'll follow up on autoscaler audit.

elena: leaving a quick config snippet for the autoscaler change in follow-up PR: 
```yaml
autoScaler:
  stabilizationWindowSeconds: 180
  scaleDownStabilization: 240
  targetCPUUtilizationPercentage: 80
```

sam_sre: closing thread — we'll reconvene in the postmortem meeting. If anyone has additional evidence (traces/logs) drop them into the incident ticket.
